masteryZone.sol: Sound waves in air are longitudinal mechanical waves, requiring a medium and propagating via compressions and rarefactions.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The speed of sound is faster in humid air than in dry air.
masteryZone.sol: True. Humid air has a lower density than dry air because water vapor is lighter than nitrogen and oxygen. Since v ∝ 1/√ρ, sound travels faster in humid air.

masteryZone.q: The frequency range of infrasonic waves is below ________ Hz.
masteryZone.sol: Infrasonic waves have frequencies below 20 Hz, which is below the human hearing limit.

masteryZone.q: A rear-view mirror in vehicles always forms:
masteryZone.sol: Convex mirrors are used for rear-view because they always form virtual, erect, and diminished images, providing a wide field of view.

masteryZone.q: An object is placed at focus of a concave mirror. Where is the image formed?
opts: Between Focus and Center of Curvature
masteryZone.sol: When the object is at focus of a concave mirror, the reflected rays are parallel and meet at infinity. The image is real, inverted, and highly magnified.

masteryZone.q: Which optical phenomenon is responsible for the working of optical fibers?
masteryZone.sol: Optical fibers work on the principle of Total Internal Reflection (TIR), trapping light signals inside the core.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Sparkling of diamond is primarily due to scattering of light.
masteryZone.sol: False. Sparkling of diamond is due to Total Internal Reflection (TIR) combined with its high refractive index and dispersion.

masteryZone.q: Myopia or Nearsightedness is corrected by using which lens?
masteryZone.sol: Myopia is corrected using a concave (diverging) lens to bring the focus back onto the retina.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Hypermetropia is corrected using a concave lens.
masteryZone.sol: False. Hypermetropia (farsightedness) is corrected using a convex (converging) lens.

opts: Dispersion of light through cloud water droplets
masteryZone.sol: Rayleigh scattering states that shorter wavelengths (blue) scatter much more than longer ones (red) by air molecules, making sky blue.
